transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-05
Start time (UTC): 15:30
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM), Samira Khan (NimbleRetail Lead Engineer), Tom Whitaker (NimbleRetail DevOps), Priya Rao (NimbleRetail PM)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Goal: Walk through Redwood SDK quickstart for Python/TypeScript, provisioning API keys, CI integration pattern, and onboarding steps for a short POC.
- Discussed host vs dedicated credentials, ephemeral sandbox keys, and secrets management for CI.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide sandbox creds + CI example repo; NimbleRetail to validate with their CI and give feedback.

Topics:
- SDK auth patterns (service key vs ephemeral tokens)
- Environment setup and secrets in CI
- Quick local dev flow + sample repo structure
- Metrics to capture (latency, token cost, error rates)
- Security review triggers and POC timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): ok everyone can hear me? good morning, afternoon depending where you are. thanks for making time. we're going to walk through the quickstart for our SDKs, focus on auth and CI provisioning. feel free to interrupt.
[00:22] Samira (NimbleRetail): yep we can hear you, thanks. we basically want a fast path to try it with a small feature flagged POC, so we're interested in how keys and secrets work in our CircleCI pipeline.
[00:34] Maya: perfect, that aligns. quick intros? arjun will lead the SDK bits, and lina will cover onboarding support and docs.
[00:40] Arjun (Redwood SE): hey all. quick checklist up front: local quickstart (python + ts), how to store keys for dev vs CI, a CI job example that doesn't leak keys, and a note about using ephemeral tokens for tighter security.
[00:55] Tom (DevOps): one thing — we use GitHub Actions for most repos, but our infra team is evaluating GitLab Runners for a specific pipeline. secrets are stored in our vault, HashiCorp Vault, and we prefer not to copy keys into environment variables that end up in logs.
[01:10] Arjun: totally. we often recommend using short-lived tokens or our CI-only service principals, and then retrieving them at job runtime from Vault. we have an example workflow that calls Vault and then injects the key into the Redwood CLI at runtime. i'll show that.
[01:25] Priya (PM): timeline wise we want a basic end-to-end prototype in two weeks, and then a security review by infra in the following week. is that feasible?
[01:34] Lina (CSM): absolutely, that's the typical cadence. we'll also provide the security questionnaire and SOC2 docs as part of the POC pack.
[01:42] Samira: great — any differences between the python and typescript SDKs we should be aware of for CI? like additional build steps, transitive deps?
[01:50] Arjun: the APIs mirror each other pretty closely; python is a tiny bit lighter to install but both are single-package installs. in CI we suggest pinning to the build artifact version (we'll share exact pins) and using our CLI for auth helper steps. typescript may need node version pinned in the action.
[02:10] Maya: ok i'll demo the quickstart repo. arjun will run through the python quickstart then the ts example.
[02:20] [screen share starts]
[02:30] Arjun: (narrating) here's the repo layout: /examples/python/quickstart.md, /examples/ts/quickstart.md, .github/workflows/redwood-ci.yml, scripts/get-sandbox-key.sh. the get-sandbox-key.sh is just a helper that calls our onboarding endpoint to mint an ephemeral key tied to the email address you signed up with.
[03:00] Samira: the ephemeral key has an expiry?
[03:05] Arjun: yes default 24 hours for sandbox, configurable for enterprise.
[03:08] Tom: our Vault rotates secrets every 7 days, so we'll want to align. any issues with rotating the Redwood key that often?
[03:18] Arjun: no, our SDK handles reconnects and will fail gracefully on invalid keys; you can program the CI to fetch a new key each run. that's why we prefer short-lived tokens in CI.
[03:30] [minor crosstalk / laughter]
[03:42] Arjun: demo — python quickstart: virtualenv, pip install redwood-client, export REDWOOD_API_KEY=..., python examples/chat_demo.py. the chat_demo shows token usage, and we include a small harness to record token cost per call.
[04:05] Samira: do you ship a helper to redact logs? we need to ensure api keys are never printed in logs.
[04:12] Arjun: yes, by default our CLI masks keys and the example logger strips envvar prints, but it's also on CI side to limit echo statements. we'll flag the script to set +x suppression.
[04:30] Priya: curious about rate limits — for POC volume small but want to know how throttling looks.
[04:36] Maya: good call. hosted accounts get a baseline rate; if you hit it we'll either increase for the POC or suggest batch patterns. also consider our dedicated if you'd need steady high throughput, but that's a later conversation.
[04:50] Samira: cost visibility is key — can we get token-level cost breakdowns in the console or via API?
[04:58] Lina: yes, console shows token-level breakdowns per API key and per route. we can give you read-only access to an example org dashboard.
[05:10] Tom: back to CI, can you show the GitHub Action snippet?
[05:15] Arjun: sure — open .github/workflows/redwood-ci.yml. [reads] name: Redwood CI; on: [push]; jobs: build: runs-on: ubuntu-latest; steps: - name: Checkout - uses: actions/checkout@v3; - name: Retrieve key from Vault - run: | export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(vault kv get -field=api_key secret/redwood/poc); - name: Run tests - run: python -m pytest --redwood-key $REDWOOD_API_KEY. note: we include a helper to fetch from Vault via OIDC or wrapped tokens so the secret isn't in the repo.
[06:00] Tom: ok that aligns. any constraints on the API key length or characters that break our secrets tooling?
[06:08] Arjun: our keys are URL-safe base64, no newlines. should work with most vaults. if you need custom encoding we can add a wrapper.
[06:20] Samira: what about local dev — is it okay to use a longer-lived developer key? we want devs to iterate without calling Vault every minute.
[06:28] Arjun: dev keys are longer-lived by default but labeled and auditable. we recommend using role-based keys: developer keys for personal dev (scoped), CI keys for pipelines (ephemeral).
[06:40] [15 second pause / typing sounds]
[06:56] Priya: security will need SSO and SCIM info. do you support SAML SSO for the console?
[07:02] Lina: yes we do SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning is available on enterprise plans. we'll attach the security pack and SSO docs after this call.
[07:12] Samira: any gotchas with private deployments or VPC when it comes to SDK config? we might later look at a private instance.
[07:20] Maya: for private deployments you generally point the SDK to your private endpoint and use the same key patterns; the main differences are network egress and cert handling. our docs include steps for custom CA and cert bundles.
[07:35] Tom: and observability — we want traces for token latency and per-call breakdowns. what agents do you support?
[07:43] Arjun: our SDK emits structured telemetry and we have plugins for Datadog and OpenTelemetry exporters. the console ingests traces so you get per-request latency and token counts.
[07:55] Samira: could you show the quick CI-run logs so we know what to expect?
[08:00] [Arjun switches to example CI run video]
[08:15] Arjun: here's a sample run: job starts, fetch vault secret, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run unit tests, run a redwood smoke test that calls the chat endpoint with a canned prompt, we assert ok and parse cost. logs show masked key values. note the smoke test uses a small token budget via header to limit cost.
[08:45] Samira: nice. can we set budget limits per API key?
[08:50] Maya: yes, we can set daily/weekly quotas and alerts. also webhook for cost burn alerts.
[08:58] Tom: one more infra question — we need to know what data is stored by default. are prompt logs retained?
[09:05] Lina: default retention for hosted is 30 days for logs, you can configure retention or disable debug logging. for enterprise we can do custom retention and redact logs. we'll include log retention options in the pack.
[09:20] Priya: ok this is helpful. Arjun, can you walk through the TS quickstart differences?
[09:26] Arjun: sure — ts example has node 18 LTS recommended, use npm ci, install @redwood/inference, set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, and run node examples/chat.ts. typescript example compiles but we also provide pre-built JS so CI doesn't need tsc on every run.
[09:45] Samira: do you have a sample jest integration test that asserts behavior and cost?
[09:50] Arjun: yes it's in examples/ts/tests/redwood.integration.test.js, it mocks network for unit tests and has an e2e smoke with a small token budget. we'll share the repo link.
[10:05] [short silence, notes being typed]
[10:20] Tom: about the sandbox key — is there an API to mint for specific scopes? e.g., read-only embeddings or generation only?
[10:28] Arjun: yes tokens can be scoped by capability (embeddings-only, read, generate) and by route. for POC we usually give generate+embeddings.
[10:40] Maya: quick demo of creating a scoped token via the onboarding endpoint (simplified): curl -X POST onboarding.redwood.ai/mint -d '{"scopes":["generate"],"ttl":86400}'. you'll get back a short key. in prod you'd bind it to an org and set RBAC.
[11:05] Samira: perfect. any limitations on model selection in sandbox? we saw some odd performance numbers in public benchmarks vs your dedicated profiles.
[11:14] Arjun: sandbox uses hosted general models; for heavy performance profiling we'd recommend a dedicated trial node so you can get exact latency numbers. for initial functional tests hosted is fine.
[11:28] Priya: let's talk timeline — we aim to have the smoke test green in two weeks. then infra security review. is there anything else we need to prep?
[11:36] Lina: please fill this short onboarding form — it asks for CI provider, expected QPS, and security contacts. we'll use it to provision the sandbox org.
[11:45] Tom: will do. question — how do rollbacks work if a model version introduces regressions? is there a pinning mechanism?
[11:54] Arjun: yes model version pinning is supported in the API and console; you can pin per-route and roll back to a previous model id instantly. we also provide canary rollout controls.
[12:08] Samira: that helps. Maya, any pricing notes we should be aware of for POC?
[12:15] Maya: POC usage is typically covered under a credit arrangement; we'll propose temporary uplift if you need more tokens. main cost levers are sequence length, batching in CI, and model choice. we'll send a simple cost-estimate sheet.
[12:30] [Wrap-up section]
[12:32] Maya: recap — action items: we'll send sandbox creds, quickstart repo, security docs; NimbleRetail will run the CI run and feedback; schedule security deep dive if infra requests.
[12:44] Priya: sounds good. can we get a short recorded screen share of the CI flow? that'd help our infra team.
[12:50] Arjun: yes we'll upload a 6-min clip and the exact workflow file.
[12:54] Samira: thanks everyone, this was productive.
[12:57] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts. chat if anything urgent. bye.

End of transcript.
